tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read UTF-8 file lines (0-based offset, default/max 2000 lines, ~48 KiB model budget, returns 1-based line numbers and file revision). Read whole small/medium files at once and page large files via next_offset; use read_tool_output for clipped captured text. Image paths (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp, <=5 MiB) return image content + revision/dimensions (non-vision models receive metadata only).

path.description: Relative to the session worktree, with forward slashes; with Full permission, an absolute path may name a file elsewhere

limit.description: Requested rows; each response has an independent output budget and may return a continuation

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a complete UTF-8 file up to 1 MiB. Pass the revision from read_file to replace a file; omit it or pass null to create a new file without replacing an existing entry. Missing parent directories are created for new files. A conflict requires reading the current file before another edit. Prefer edit_file for partial changes and larger files.

path.description: Relative to the session worktree, with forward slashes; with Full permission, an absolute path may name a file elsewhere

expected_revision.description: Revision to replace; omit or null to create

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Edit one UTF-8 file read in this conversation. Pass old_text/new_text or edits (never both). Each old_text must match uniquely unless replace_all is true. Fails atomically on overlap, missing match, or stale revision; returns updated revision and edited hunks.

path.description: Relative to the session worktree, with forward slashes; with Full permission, an absolute path may name a file elsewhere

expected_revision.description: Optional; defaults to the revision last seen in this conversation

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Add, update, move or delete files under one approval. Prefer edit_file or write_file for a single-file edit.
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: a
+one
*** Update File: b
@@ anchor
 context
-old
+new
*** Delete File: c
*** End Patch
Prefix added lines with +, including every line of a new file. Update context (space), removals (-) and optional @@ anchors must match the current file exactly at one location, including whitespace. An additions-only hunk inserts right after that line, or at EOF with bare @@. *** Move to: renames and creates missing directories. *** End of File anchors a hunk at EOF. Read every file you update, move or delete first. A prior write counts. If a file changed since you read it, read it again. Up to 16 files are validated before anything is written, counting a moved and edited file twice. Validation failure rejects all with per-file reasons. Writes then proceed in order and stop on failure without rolling back earlier files. Each file reports applied, failed, unknown or not_attempted. Inspect an unknown file before retrying.

input.description: The whole patch from *** Begin Patch to *** End Patch, with paths relative to the session worktree; with Full permission, absolute paths may name files elsewhere on one volume

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find worktree-relative file paths by globs (default root), honoring .gitignore and skipping symlinks. Sorted newest-first; default/max 500 paths per page via next_offset. No shell approval needed.

path.description: Worktree-relative file or directory; empty or . selects the root. With Full permission, an absolute path may name one elsewhere

limit.description: Requested rows; each response has an independent output budget and may return a continuation

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search UTF-8 files with embedded ripgrep (honors .gitignore, skips symlinks/binaries, no approval needed). Modes: files, content, or count; supports globs (! excludes) and multiline. Up to 200 rows/page (~32 KiB budget); paginate via next_offset or narrow path on 20s timeout.

query.description: Text or regex to match in files. Globs filter paths.

path.description: Worktree-relative file or directory; empty or . selects the root. With Full permission, an absolute path may name one elsewhere

limit.description: Requested rows; each response has an independent output budget and may return a continuation

tools.name: read_office
tools.description: Read DOCX/PDF text, XLSX cell values and formulas, or PPTX slide text and notes from a worktree path or an attachment visible in this conversation. Use source.kind "path" with a worktree-relative path, or "attachment" with its attachment ID. Earlier attachments must belong to completed, failed or cancelled turns still visible in this conversation; queued or running future inputs are unavailable. Images and scanned PDF pages use OCR when an OCR model is installed on the Node. File sources return the revision for edits. Follow next offsets to read every section, including continuations of long parts.

value.description: Worktree-relative path or visible conversation attachment ID

offset.description: Zero-based section offset. Long document parts continue in subsequent sections.

tools.name: read_notebook
tools.description: Read numbered nbformat 4 cells without executing a kernel. Use next_offset to continue. Returned cell JSON retains source, metadata and saved outputs; truncated cells omit oversized content and include a bounded source preview.

limit.description: Requested rows; each response has an independent output budget and may return a continuation

tools.name: edit_notebook
tools.description: Apply a revision-checked atomic batch to nbformat 4 cells. Replace changes only source and retains the cell ID, metadata and saved outputs. Insert creates a cell with a new ID; delete removes a cell. Zero-based indices refer to the original notebook; multiple inserts at the same index preserve batch order. Read the notebook first. No kernel is executed.

expected_revision.description: Optional; defaults to the revision last seen in this conversation

instructions: Prefer find_files, search_files, read_file, edit_file and apply_patch over shell commands, and batch independent reads in one turn. Read a worktree image with read_file when you need to see it; read_office extracts document text and reads conversation attachments.
